items.title: Group Japa
items.speaker: Śrīla Prabhupāda
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Listen to His Divine Grace Śrīla Prabhupāda himself chanting japa
in a group with disciples. This is not a lecture *about* chanting
— it is the sound of the founder-ācārya chanting. Play it once
before your morning rounds and let the cadence, pronunciation,
and mood inform your own. Nothing instructs japa more than this.
items.source: ISKCON Desire Tree Audio Archive — Śrīla Prabhupāda Japa folder

items.title: Japa by Example
items.speaker: Śrīla Prabhupāda
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
The second of Śrīla Prabhupāda's two preserved japa recordings —
a model of attentive chanting at brāhma-muhūrta pace. Use this
not as background music but as a pre-japa tuning fork: listen
once, then begin your own rounds at the same pace, with the same
precision of each syllable.
items.source: ISKCON Desire Tree Audio Archive — Śrīla Prabhupāda Japa folder

items.title: Japa Class — Vṛndāvana 2011-01-07
items.speaker: HG Bhurijana Prabhu
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Bhurijana Prabhu's Vṛndāvana japa classes are among the clearest
step-by-step instructions on raising attention during rounds —
the four-step technique (saṅkalpa → neglect the mind → take
shelter → await mercy) is unpacked plainly. Listen once before
morning japa for direct application.

items.title: The Mind and the Holy Name — Israel 2005-01-01
items.speaker: HG Bhurijana Prabhu
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
One of Bhurijana Prabhu's most cited lectures on japa: the
relationship between the wandering mind and the Holy Name, with
concrete practices for keeping the mind from rebelling against
the round. A clean, considered class to anchor a week of japa.

items.title: Chanting Workshop — Melbourne 2006-05-04
items.speaker: HG Bhurijana Prabhu
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
A live workshop format — Bhurijana Prabhu working through
chanting difficulties with the audience in real time. Useful when
you want practical Q&A-style instruction rather than a
monologue. Especially relevant for householders who face time
pressure and mind-wandering during rounds.

items.title: Śikṣāṣṭakam — Israel 2006-01-04
items.speaker: HG Bhurijana Prabhu
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Bhurijana Prabhu on the Śikṣāṣṭakam — the eight verses Lord
Caitanya left as His instruction on chanting. Direct treatment
of the verse-by-verse mood progression. Pair this lecture with
the weekly verse if the rotation lands on a Śikṣāṣṭakam quote.

items.title: Holy Name & Japa Mood lectures (Theme-wise)
items.speaker: HH Rādhānātha Swami
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Rādhānātha Swami's lectures on the Holy Name interweave
Mahābhārata and Bhāgavatam pastimes (Ajāmila, Gajendra,
Haridāsa Ṭhākura) with concrete sādhana counsel. Most useful
when your faith in chanting itself needs renewing through
storytelling. Browse the Theme-wise → Holy Name section for the
specific mood-on-chanting lectures.

items.title: Holy Name retreat lectures
items.speaker: HH Sacinandana Swami
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Sacinandana Swami's retreat lectures are the closest thing in
modern ISKCON to a sustained meditation manual for japa — Two
Doors (mechanical chanting vs. calling out with love), the
three-step opening, concrete methods to bring the mind to the
heart before chanting.

items.title: Japa workshops
items.speaker: HG Mahātmā Prabhu
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Mahātmā Prabhu's lectures are deliberately practical — short
techniques, immediately applicable, free of grand language.
Especially useful when your japa has gone mechanical and you
need a small lever to change it tomorrow.

items.title: Glories of the Holy Name
items.speaker: HH Bhakti Cāru Swami
items.why_it_helps_chanting:
Bhakti Cāru Swami's voice and pacing themselves are an aid to
chanting mood. His CC lectures dwell on the līlā of the Name's
appearance through Lord Caitanya — the lineage gratitude this
generates is itself a japa-mood stabilizer.
